label: Weapon delivery
description: How a shot reaches its target.

terms.label: Hitscan
terms.description: Hits instantly along the line of fire.

terms.label: Projectile
terms.description: A visible shot with travel time that can be dodged.

terms.label: Beam
terms.description: A continuous beam held on the target; the effect builds while it stays on.

terms.label: Lobbed
terms.description: Indirect fire: the shot arcs over cover onto a ground point, or lands on a target the shooter cannot see itself, which others must spot. Usually slow to land, often with a minimum range. It never hits fliers.

terms.label: Lock-on
terms.description: Hold on a target to lock, then fire homing shots; the target gets a warning.

terms.label: Guided
terms.description: You steer the shot in flight by keeping your aim on it; it is lost if you stop aiming, so the shooter stays exposed until it lands. It reaches whatever its family reaches.
terms.notes: The player does the steering, so it needs a mount the player aims (not auto-target or radial) and no homing trait, and it is a medium-range or longer shot. A shot that steers itself after a lock is lock-on; one that steers itself with no lock step is projectile with the homing trait.
examples: Battlefield: TOW missiles follow the gunner's crosshair until they hit
Battlefield: the attack helicopter gunner flies the TV-guided missile through its camera

terms.label: Melee
terms.description: Strikes or lunges at touching distance.

terms.label: Attach
terms.description: Works by latching onto or getting inside the target.

terms.label: Place
terms.description: Sets down charges, mines or devices on the ground or a target. What is placed stays on the ground, so it never hits fliers; a charge that clings to a flier is attach.

terms.label: Drop
terms.description: Released below or just ahead of the unit; you aim by flying over the target, so only a flier can drop. It falls to the ground, so it never hits fliers.

terms.label: Ram / kamikaze
terms.description: The unit itself is the weapon: it hits by colliding with or diving into the target, often destroying itself.

tie_breaks.rule: Lock-on when the target is chosen before firing and the shot then finds it alone, so the shooter may look away; the target is usually warned. A missile that homes on a laser spot is lock-on when a teammate's designator also works. Guided when only the shooter steers it and must keep aiming until it lands: by wire, camera, crosshair or the shooter's own laser. When one entry stands for several titles of a series that differ, follow the Series games convention and give the other version in the summary.
